pages.quiz:
ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #20
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.

2. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.

3. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. happiness
   C. blue
   D. run

4. When practising Language School, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Language School.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Language School.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Language School.

5. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.

6. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.

7. When practising Pre Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pre Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Pre Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Pre Reading.

8. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. went
   C. goes
   D. going

9. When practising Language Welcome and, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Language Welcome and.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Language Welcome and.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Language Welcome and.

10. When practising Phonics, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Phonics.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Phonics.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Phonics.

11. When practising Pre-Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-Writing.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Pre-Writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pre-Writing.

12. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. No full stops

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Pre Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Phonics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Word Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Connected text and fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:

====

2. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

3. D — run

7. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.

8. B — went

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.

10. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.

11. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.

12. A — One main idea with supporting sentences

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pre Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Phonics; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Word Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Connected text and fluency; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
